stem: A client on the kidney-transplant waiting list says, "I am anxious because I do not know when an organ offer will come." Which nursing response is best?

options.A: Acknowledge the uncertainty, encourage the client to discuss personal waitlist status and medical questions with the transplant team, provide reliable transplant information, and offer support-group or peer resources if the client wants them.
options.B: Reassure the client that an organ offer should occur within a predictable short period because waiting time alone determines when a kidney becomes available.
options.C: Avoid discussing the waiting process because uncertainty is best managed by giving the client as little transplant information as possible.
options.D: Tell the client that anxiety is unwarranted once listed because being on the national waitlist guarantees that a suitable kidney will be offered.

rationale: Current HRSA/OPTN kidney-transplant resources explain that waiting-list care involves ongoing appointments and communication with the transplant program and that organ offers depend on multiple matching and allocation factors rather than a predictable waiting-time guarantee. HRSA also directs candidates to their transplant team for questions about their own medical care or waitlist status and provides OPTN patient information resources for general transplant questions. Its kidney-transplant FAQ specifically notes that doctors, patient support groups, and other people who have been treated for kidney disease can provide information and support. Therefore, A is correct. B creates false certainty, C withholds useful support and information, and D incorrectly treats listing as a guarantee of transplantation.
educational_objective: Support transplant-waitlist anxiety with therapeutic acknowledgment, accurate information, appropriate transplant-team communication, and optional peer/support resources without giving false predictions or guarantees about organ availability.
source_organization: Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) / Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN)
source_document_title: Frequently Asked Questions About Kidney Transplant Evaluation and Listing; Patient Information Letter; Transplant Process
source_version_date: Current HRSA/OPTN patient resources; Patient Information Letter reviewed December 2025
source_locator: HRSA/OPTN Kidney Transplant FAQ → treatment decisions and transplant learning: doctors, patient support groups, and other people treated for kidney disease can provide information; while listed, candidates must maintain regular appointments so the transplant team can monitor condition. HRSA/OPTN Patient Information Letter → OPTN patient services provides general transplant/waiting-list information, but personal medical care and waitlist status questions belong to the transplant hospital. HRSA Transplant Process/Allocation resources → organ offers depend on organ-specific matching/allocation factors and transplant-team review, not a guaranteed fixed wait time.
source_claim_supported: Directly supports accurate information, transplant-team communication, and support-group/peer resources for kidney-transplant candidates while excluding promises about when an organ offer will occur.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity → Anxiety/Coping/Therapeutic Communication/Support Systems: acknowledge uncertainty, provide accurate information, support coping, and facilitate appropriate social or peer resources during prolonged illness-related waiting periods.
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — coping with kidney-transplant waitlist uncertainty
correction_summary: Updated the source from older UNOS wording to current federal HRSA/OPTN patient resources. The final item keeps the useful psychosocial construct but removes any implication that waitlist duration is predictable or that listing guarantees transplant. It anchors support to accurate information, transplant-team communication, and optional patient-support/peer resources explicitly recognized by HRSA.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Anxiety and coping during kidney-transplant waitlisting
audit_findings.source_authority: Current federal HRSA/OPTN patient guidance rather than legacy standalone UNOS educational material.
audit_findings.currentness: HRSA/OPTN patient resources were reviewed/updated through December 2025 and remain current at the 2026 audit date.

claim_by_claim.stem: Uncertainty about timing of an organ offer is clinically coherent because allocation depends on multiple factors and no fixed offer date can be guaranteed.
claim_by_claim.A: Correct because it uses therapeutic acknowledgment, directs personal status questions to the transplant team, and offers reliable information and support resources.
claim_by_claim.B: Incorrect because waiting time is only one factor and no predictable short waiting interval can be promised.
claim_by_claim.C: Incorrect because HRSA provides extensive patient education and support resources; withholding information does not support informed coping.
claim_by_claim.D: Incorrect because listing does not guarantee that or when a suitable organ will be offered.
claim_by_claim.rationale: Does not claim that every anxious candidate needs formal mental-health treatment or a specific support group.
claim_by_claim.educational_objective: Specific to therapeutic support under transplant waitlist uncertainty.

audit_findings.distractor_audit: B offers false prediction, C avoids useful communication, and D gives false reassurance/guarantee. Each is realistic and distinct.
audit_findings.ambiguity_and_second_answer: Only A is both emotionally supportive and factually consistent with current transplant-system information.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are nursing responses to the same waitlist-anxiety statement and use comparable structure.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is directly appropriate because the item tests anxiety, coping, therapeutic communication, and support resources.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited whether 'peer support' is directly supported by current federal guidance. HRSA's kidney FAQ explicitly identifies patient support groups and other people treated for kidney disease as information/support sources. The final wording makes peer support optional rather than mandatory. No unresolved conflict remains.
